real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to furry dogs (and dog-like animals such as wolves and lesser pandas), and it is weakest when the animal faces or points to the left. It is more active when the subject faces right, faces toward or away from the camera, or has no clear facing direction. It also prefers subjects that fill much of the frame and are centered, and it is suppressed by a cool blue or green tint.

real_s2.explanation: Across these dog and wolf classes, the unit's clearest particular trait is that it responds weakly when the main animal faces or points to the left. It is more active for right-facing animals, for animals facing toward or away from the camera, and for photos with no single clear facing direction. It also prefers large, centered, frame-filling subjects and warm rather than cool color casts, but the similar units largely share those preferences.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to dog and furry-canid faces (fluffy dogs, wolves, lesser panda). It is noticeably weaker when the animal faces left. Its strongest distinctive signal is the left/right facing asymmetry: it is more active for right-facing or frontal subjects than for left-facing ones. It also favors large, centered subjects and warm rather than cool color casts, but those preferences are largely shared with similar units.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to furry dogs and dog-like animals (small long-haired terriers and toy breeds, spitz types, wolves, lesser panda). Within these classes it is somewhat more active when the animal sits centered and fully inside the frame, in scenes with a level horizon or straight lines (indoor or structured surroundings) rather than a featureless background, under medium rather than bright light. Most effects are weak. The only rows near or above the 95th percentile are the level-lines contrast, the central placement and the fully-in-frame contrast, and the similar units are mostly not unusual on these rows.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds mainly to fluffy dogs and dog-like animals (toy breeds, terriers, spitz types, wolves, lesser panda). Within those classes it is somewhat more active when the animal is centered and fully inside the frame and when level straight lines such as floors, furniture or a horizon are visible. It is less active on close-up crops with no lines and on subjects facing sideways. Every row is weak, and only the level-lines row reaches the 95th percentile.

null_s3.explanation: The unit responds to fluffy, long-haired dogs, mostly small terriers and toy breeds, along with wolves and the lesser panda. Within those classes, the photo properties barely change its activity. It is somewhat more active when the animal is centered, fully inside the frame, and set against a scene with visible level straight lines or a horizon rather than a plain featureless background. It is also somewhat more active when there is no single clearly facing subject, but that answer had only 6 photos. Row 17 is the only one at the 95th percentile, and the similar units are not high there. Rows 11 and 10 are close behind and are also low for the similar units. Row 12 is excluded because the similar units score high on it, so it reflects something they share.
